article_title: New Approaches to Continuing Medical Education: a QStream (spaced education) Program for Research Translation in Ovarian Cancer.
citation: Robinson Tracy, Janssen Anna, Kirk Judy, DeFazio Anna, Goodwin Annabel, Tucker Kathy, Shaw Timothy. (2017). New Approaches to Continuing Medical Education: a QStream (spaced education) Program for Research Translation in Ovarian Cancer. Journal of Cancer Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s13187-015-0944-7
title: QStream spaced education model: case-based questions emailed at spaced intervals with succinct corrective feedback
description: QStream (previously spaced education), developed at Harvard Medical School, delivers case-based multiple-choice questions electronically over several weeks. 'Upon answering a question, participants are given succinct feedback and links to further resources.' It exploits the finding that 'educational encounters which are spaced and repeated over time result in more efficient learning and improved learning retention'. Typical programs repeat cases in cycles of 8 to 45 days; this study used only three case scenarios.
requirements: Participants answer each question correctly on two occasions before it is retired; the course is completed when all questions are retired
constraints: Given the brief nature of the guideline changes, the current study relied on only three case scenarios rather than the at least eight typical of QStream programs
target_learners: senior clinicians (gynaecological and medical oncologists, their trainees, and nurses)
target_learning_goals: updated knowledge of clinical guideline criteria for genetic assessment and referral of women with ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
examples: The pilot program sent incorrect-answer questions again 5 days later and correct-answer questions 8 days later

New Approaches to Continuing Medical Education: a QStream (spaced education) Program for Research Translation in Ovarian Cancer. citation: C. Savage, D. McGrath, T. McIntyre, M. Wegener, M. Williamson. (2009). Teaching Physics Using Virtual Reality. http://realtimerelativity.org
title: QSim: a prototype simulation visualizing the single-particle wavefunction evolving under the Schrödinger equation
description: QSim is a prototype quantum dynamics simulation that visualizes the single-particle wavefunction, chosen despite disagreement in the field about its ontological status. "The simulation evolves the wavefunction in time according to the Schrödinger equation" and "implements discrete position measurements with variable resolution", enabling repeated automated position measurements with specified frequency and number, plotted in three-dimensional space. This supports investigation of the quantum Zeno effect at the introductory level.
requirements: Requires deciding what will be visualized; unlike Real Time Relativity, which visualized what would be seen by the eye or a camera, QSim visualizes mathematics if the wavefunction is regarded as a mathematical abstraction
constraints: Development is at prototype stage, evaluated so far only with six third-year students rather than the introductory-level target students
target_learners: introductory-level quantum mechanics students (piloted with third-year physics students)
target_learning_goals: quantum dynamics, quantum measurement, the wavefunction, the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, and the quantum Zeno effect
examples: Pilot lab activities were free evolution of the wavefunction, position measurement, and the quantum Zeno effect; students wrote that the visual representation helps build a mental picture of what is happening in quantum mechanics
key_sources: C. Savage, D. McGrath, T. McIntyre, M. Wegener, M. Williamson. (2009). Teaching Physics Using Virtual Reality. https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.5776
